points.description: Describes backpropagation as propagating the error backwards through the network layer by layer (from the last layer towards the first), updating the weights at each layer to reduce the error. Equivalent wording such as 'recursively backwards from output to input' or 'error flows back through the layers and weights are adjusted' earns the mark.

States that the weight updates are driven by local gradients computed with partial derivatives of the error and the chain rule. Mentioning only 'gradients' or 'derivatives' without the chain rule, or only 'chain rule' without linking it to the gradient/weight update, does not earn the mark. Equivalent correct technical terms earn the mark.
